title: The Sound of Philadelphia
summary: Celebrate 50 Years of The Sound of Philadelphia at the Royal Albert Hall!
body_text: The Sound of Philadelphia Join us on Saturday 19th October for an unforgettable night at London’s iconic Royal Albert Hall, as Sir Lenny Henry presents ‘ The Sound of Philadelphia ’, a special concert celebrating 50 years of Philly soul music. This one night only event marks the golden anniversary of the release of the seminal track TSOP ( The Sound of Philadelphia ), a song that defined an entire genre. The evening will honor the legendary songwriting talents of Kenny Gamble, Leon Huff, and Thom Bell, three pioneers of the Philadelphia International Records label, which revolutionized soul music with its rich blend of funk, lush string arrangements, and smooth melodies. Philadelphia International Records, founded in 1971, is credited with shaping the Philly soul sound and laying the foundation for disco music in the 1970s. A star-studded lineup of special guest singers, including Beverley Knight, Andrew Roachford, Omar Lye-Fook, Tony Momrelle, Ashton Jones, Derek Green, and Wayne Ellington—will take the stage, accompanied by the BBC Concert Orchestra under the musical direction of Chris Cameron. Expect to hear classic hits such as Ain't No Stoppin' Us Now, Love Train, Me and Mrs. Jones, and many more from the label’s legendary back catalogue. Don’t miss this opportunity to relive the magic of Philly soul and celebrate its lasting legacy. Book your tickets now for an evening that promises to be a soulful journey through one of music’s most influential eras. Event Details: Date: Saturday, 19th October Location: Royal Albert Hall, London Tickets: here Celebrate the timeless sound of Philadelphia – a night of soul you won't forget!

title: Texxon Holding Limited Announces Commencement of Operations at Henan Polystyrene Production Facility, A Milestone in Manufacturing Expansion Strategy
summary: The Henan facility can produce up to 600,000 tons a year and serves GPPS and HIPS products for appliance and consumer applications.
body_text: Texxon Holding (Nasdaq:NPT) began operations at its new Henan polystyrene production facility in June 2026, completing construction and commissioning. The plant in Taiqian County, Henan, has up to 600,000 tons annual capacity and supports GPPS and HIPS production for appliance and consumer goods markets. The facility is located within a major manufacturing and logistics corridor, within a 500-km radius of key home appliance hubs, and has passed required safety, environmental and regulatory inspections. Texxon views this as a key step in its shift toward an integrated manufacturing and supply chain platform.

body_text: Under Armour today welcomes Christina Najjar, better known as Tinx, as its newest brand ambassador, representing both UA footwear and apparel. A creator, entrepreneur, bestselling author, and one of the most influential voices shaping modern conversations around confidence, wellness, and self-worth, Tinx joins the UA family as the brand continues to broaden its definition of performance. The partnership begins with Summer of Outside , a new event series inspired by the movement Tinx created and her annual commitment to spend less time on her phone, and spend more time outdoors, prioritizing human connection, and doing the things that make her feel her best. The series will make stops in San Francisco, Chicago, and New York City, bringing together movement, community, and the rituals Tinx has become famous for. Each meet up will feature movement, product giveaways, Christina’s Café pop-up experience, and moments designed for attendees to disconnect, recharge, and leave feeling better than when they arrived.

body_text: Selected as one of three late-breakthrough abstracts: clinical trials and innovation in thrombosis, CAD-1005 took center stage before the global thrombosis community at the largest ISTH meeting in more than a decade. Oral presentation by Principal Investigator Dr. Steven E. McKenzie highlighted CAD-1005 as the first randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled trial for Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT). Phase 2 data demonstrate an absolute reduction of more than 25% in thrombotic events, supporting the clinical advancement of this Phase 3-ready program. CAD-1005 targets a life-threatening immune-mediated clotting disorder, with an estimated $2 billion in peak annual revenue and no currently approved root-cause therapies. PARIS, July 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Cadrenal Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: CVKD), a late-stage biopharmaceutical company advancing novel therapies for rare immunothrombotic conditions, announced today that late-breaking clinical data from the Phase 2 study of the first-in-class 12-lipoxygenase (12-LOX) inhibitor CAD-1005 were featured in a highly anticipated late-breaking oral presentation at the International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis (ISTH) 2026 Congress in Paris. This year’s ISTH Congress marked a historic milestone, bringing together clinicians, researchers, scientists, educators and industry leaders from around the world for five days of scientific discovery, collaboration and innovation in thrombosis, hemostasis and vascular biology. Drawing the largest in-person audience in more than a decade, the event attracted over 6,000 registrants and more than 3,100 abstract submissions. As the premier global gathering for cutting-edge scientific research, the ISTH late-breakthrough program is reserved for high-impact clinical trial results and first disclosures that may define future standards of care and clinical practice. The oral presentation, titled “12-lipoxygenase inhibition with CAD-1005 (formerly known as VLX-1005) in heparin-induced thrombocytopenia,” was part of the high-profile session on clinical trials and breakthrough innovations. It marks a historic milestone as the first randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled clinical trial in patients with Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT). “Targeting 12-lipoxygenase is a novel, highly selective therapeutic approach that is intended to address the root cause of immune-mediated platelet activation in HIT,” said Dr. Steven E. McKenzie. “The data we presented in Paris illustrated how CAD-1005 could fundamentally shift the treatment paradigm for acute thrombotic care. By showing an encouraging reduction in thrombotic events when added to standard anticoagulation, this therapy may offer a highly differentiated and desperately needed option for these high-risk patients. Clinicians from around the world were enthusiastic about this novel approach to a serious unmet medical need.” Key Phase 2 Highlights Presented: Addressing the Root Cause: Unlike standard-of-care anticoagulants that only reduce thrombin generation, CAD-1005 is designed to directly block the underlying 12-LOX immune signaling loop that drives antibody-mediated platelet activation. Efficacy Signal: Patients treated with CAD-1005 experienced a reduction of more than 25% in new or worsening thrombotic events compared with the placebo arm (50% vs. >75%), despite the study not being sufficiently powered for statistical significance. Safety Signal: No serious adverse events attributable to CAD-1005, no major bleeding in SRA+ patients, and no deaths. Treatment with CAD-1005 was associated with fewer thromboembolic events without an increase in major bleeding. Paradigm Shift in Trial Design: The trial established that the traditional platelet count recovery rate is an inadequate surrogate for clinical efficacy, as thrombotic events continued to occur after recovery. This provides critical framework intelligence for Cadrenal’s upcoming pivotal Phase 3 registration trial. “The selection of the Phase 2 study for a late-breaking presentation at ISTH underscores the scientific integrity and significant commercial potential of CAD-1005,” said Quang X. Pham, Chief Executive Officer of Cadrenal Therapeutics. “With our recent financing, we are well-positioned to advance partnering opportunities for CAD-1005 and tecarfarin.” CAD-1005 has received Orphan Drug and Fast Track designations from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and Orphan Drug status from the European Medicines Agency (EMA). About Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT) HIT is an immune-mediated, prothrombotic adverse drug reaction in which antibodies against platelet factor 4-heparin complexes activate platelets via FcγRIIA receptors, triggering a cascade that can lead to life-threatening thrombosis. Current management relies on non-heparin anticoagulants, which reduce thrombin generation but do not directly address the underlying antibody-mediated platelet activation; new thrombosis remains a major clinical concern even with appropriate anticoagulant therapy. About CAD-1005 CAD-1005 is a novel investigational therapeutic in development for the treatment of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT). CAD-1005 is designed to selectively inhibit 12-lipoxygenase (12-LOX), an enzyme central to platelet immune activation and thrombo-inflammatory signaling in HIT. CAD-1005 is intended to be used alongside existing standards of care and is being developed to address the underlying biological mechanisms that drive disease progression. To view how CAD-1005 works in HIT, click https://vimeo.com/1209382706/7dde06dc08?share=copy&fl=sv&fe=ci About Cadrenal Therapeutics, Inc. Cadrenal Therapeutics, Inc. is a late-stage biopharmaceutical company advancing novel therapies for life-threatening immune and thrombotic conditions. Its lead program, CAD-1005, is being investigated as a first-in-class 12-LOX inhibitor for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT), a deadly immune-mediated thrombotic disorder. CAD-1005 has received Orphan Drug and Fast Track designations from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and orphan drug status from the European Medicines Agency. Second-generation 12-LOX oral therapeutics are also in development for chronic indications. The Company’s broader pipeline includes tecarfarin, a late-stage oral vitamin K antagonist designed to prevent heart attacks, strokes, and deaths from blood clots in patients requiring chronic anticoagulation, including those with end-stage kidney disease, those with left ventricular assist devices, and potentially those with Kawasaki disease (KD), an acute, self-limited, febrile illness that primarily affects children <5 years old and is the leading cause of acquired heart disease in developed countries. Tecarfarin has also received Orphan Drug and Fast Track designations from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). title: Ericsson and Transsion settle global patent litigation

body_text: Ericsson and Transsion settle global patent litigation Ericsson and global Chinese smartphone maker Transsion have reached a settlement resolving their dispute over a multi-year, global patent cross-license agreement. title: Children Eczema
summary: Discover expert insights on managing childhood eczema. Explore different types, triggers, and clinical treatment options for your child’s skin.
body_text: Children's Eczema:The Constant Worries of Flare-Ups End Where Clinical Science Begins. The struggles of parents whose children experience the discomfort of eczema flare-ups are relentless. Watching your child constantly scratching their skin, avoiding activities of life, and waking up from midnight sleep is a heartbreak no parent should go through. Children’s ec zema management requires thick creams; it needs a deeper level repair of the skin barrier and the perfectly balanced skin pH, which are known to be the biological reasons for the continuous itch-scratch cycles. In a healthy human skin, the pH is naturally acidic, around 4.5 – 4.9. In childhood eczema, the pH is often elevated to an alkaline level. The high pH activates certain enzymes that break down the skin's structural proteins, making the skin barrier weak and permeable to pathogens. even more fragile. Eczema in Children - Causes and Risk Factors What actually causes eczema in children is the first thing parents need to understand so that they can opt for the right treatment. There is no one factor behind it, but a complex interaction between genetics and the environment. One factor identified is filaggrin deficiency, which is a protein essential for maintaining a strong skin barrier . Without it, the skin's moisture escapes quite faster, and external irritants easily attack the skin, leading to the chronic dryness and sensitivity we recognize as dermatitis in children . Here is a detailed overview of common causes and risk factors for eczema in kids: Understanding why eczema in children occurs is the first step in managing it effectively. It is rarely caused by a single factor; instead, it is a complex interaction between a child’s internal biology and their external environment. Genetic Predisposition the primary biological driver of kids’ eczema Children of parents with Atopic Triad: Hay fever, Eczema and Asthma. Immune system overreactivity to certain harmless substances, such as dust mites, harsh bath products, and even stress. Environmental Triggers like low humidity in winter, extreme dry weather, synthetic fabrics, pet dander, molds, and seasonal pollens. Parents need to identify the risk factors and step forward from the temporary fixes labelled under the name of eczema treatment. Eczema in Kids: Signs and Symptoms Eczema signs and symptoms in kids or children usually vary. The need is not to confuse it with a simple rash, but to identify the early warning signs. Eczema in children often begins as patches of dry, scaly skin. Red patches that are dry, itchy (in lighter skin tones) Brown, purple, or grey patches in darker skin tone It can begin to show up on the cheeks, scalp, or creases of joints, such as the elbow, knee, and wrist. May evolve into an intense eczema rash in kids. Your child may become restless, and the very first behaviour that you will notice is constant itching, leading to an itch-scratch cycle. Increased irritability due to constant itch and discomfort. Identifying these symptoms in their infancy allows for immediate intervention, preventing the skin from breaking and reducing the risk of secondary infections. The intense itching (pruritus) seen with an eczema rash in kids often leads to: Sleep Deprivation and exhaustion for the child as well as the whole family Risk of secondary inflammation Parents must monitor these signs vigilantly to keep the symptoms manageable, short-lived, and, most importantly, keep them away for lasting relief. The result: active skin barrier repair moving beyond just moisturizing. It actively Repairs the skin barrier Regulates skin pH and resets the acid mantle Absorbs well and does not trigger sensitivities.
